item.title: Building a Phishing Email Infrastructure: Postfix, DKIM, DMARC, SMTP Relay, GoPhish & EvilGinx
item.description: Today, we’re setting up email. Those of you who are familiar with the self-hosting sphere know how much of a pain it is to set up email yourself. Hopefully, this guide will help beginner red teamers or just curious people understand the specific way I set up my phishing infrastructure. Registering a Domain Name && Setting up an Azure VM I’ll be combining Azure, Namecheap and Cloudflare for this part, but you can choose any alternatives that you like for any of these services.

item.title: Building a Custom Mythic Agent from Scratch (in Python)
item.description: This is the continuation of this article ## Introduction Now that we have a working Mythic setup, we’re able to deep diver into C2 architecture and start integrating our own tools and techniques to the base platform. The goal is simple: Understand how an agent really works internally Build my own minimal implant Extend it with a custom command tied to a real-world privilege escalation exploit Integrate everything cleanly into Mythic’s tasking system Understanding the Agent Model To get started, we have example containers available to help us understand the file structures.

item.title: Red Teaming Methodology: A Complete Overview
item.description: Red Teaming is a controlled simulation of adversarial attacks, designed to test and improve an organization’s security posture. By simulating the tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) of real attackers, Red Team exercises help organizations evaluate their ability to detect, respond to, and recover from sophisticated threats. 1. Introduction to Red Teaming The essence of Red Teaming is to think like an attacker: identify vulnerabilities, bypass defenses, and attempt unauthorized access to critical assets.
